# Page 16^page=16
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS MoCA Notifies Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 to Replace Aircraft Rules, 1937 In October 2026, the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) notified the ‘Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026’, in the Gazette of India, replacing the nearly nine-decade-old Aircraft Rules, 1937, to modernise India’s civil aviation regulatory framework. • The new rules will come into effect on 1 January 2027, introducing a consolidated regulatory framework for aircraft registration, safety certification, maintenance, flight operations, personnel licensing, airline tariffs and airport operations. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 notified ✓ Notified by: MoCA ✓ Effective from: 1 January 2027 ✓ Replace: Aircraft Rules, 1937 ✓ Regulatory Authority: DGCA ✓ Fare Disclosure: Airlines must disclose total ticket prices, including base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges and refund conditions. Key Provisions of Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026: Framework: The rules are framed under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, which establishes the regulatory framework for India’s civil aviation sector. Certification: It prescribes requirements for aircraft registration, airworthiness certification, design approval, manufacturing, modifications and repairs. Maintenance: Mandates regular aircraft inspections and maintenance to ensure continued airworthiness and compliance with safety standards. Licensing: Specifies qualification, training, examination, experience and medical fitness requirements for pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers and air traffic controllers, along with licence renewal, suspension and cancellation conditions. Operations: Regulates flight planning, operational procedures, safety standards and flight and duty time limitations for pilots and cabin crew to prevent fatigue. • It also prescribes minimum crew rest periods and covers aerodrome licensing, airport infrastructure and safety requirements. Tariffs: Requires scheduled airlines to determine fares based on factors such as operating costs and submit tariff details to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) for monitoring. • Airlines must publish fares on official websites and digital platforms and disclose the total ticket price during booking and on the booked ticket, including base fare, taxes, fees, cancellation charges and refund conditions. The rules also distinguish government taxes from airline service fees. Intervention: Empowers the Government of India (GoI) to issue written directions on airline fares during extraordinary situations when intervention is necessary in the public interest. About Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA): Establishment – Established in 1927 as the Department of Civil Aviation (DoCA), it evolved into a statutory regulatory body under the Aircraft Amendment Act, 2020. Director General (DG)– Vir Vikram Yadav Headquarters – New Delhi, Delhi MoD Signs Rs. 53,866.50 Crore Contracts for Eight Next Generation Corvettes for Indian Navy In November 2026, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) signed contracts worth Rs. 53,866.50 Crore with Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) for the construction of 8 Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for the Indian Navy (IN), to enhance the IN’s maritime capabilities and promote indigenous warship manufacturing. • The contracts were signed in the presence of Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary of MoD, at Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi, Delhi. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Contracts worth Rs. 53,866.50 crore signed for 8 NGCs. ✓ Signed By: Ministry of Defence, GRSE and GSL. ✓ Where? Kartavya Bhawan-2, New Delhi, Delhi. ✓ Purpose: Strengthening maritime capabilities and indigenous warship manufacturing. ✓ Construction Share: GRSE – 5 corvettes; GSL – 3 corvettes. ✓ Design: IN; construction by competitively selected DPSUs. ✓ Capabilities: Advanced missiles, weapons and sensor suites; air, surface and sub-surface operations. ✓ Timeline: 10 years. Highlights of the NGC Project for the Indian Navy: Shipbuilding: GRSE will construct five corvettes, while GSL will construct the remaining three. Indigenous Design: The project marks the 1st project in which warships will be indigenously designed by the IN and constructed by Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) selected through a competitive process. Capabilities: Equipped with state-of-the-art capabilities including advanced missiles, weapons and sensor suites, the NGCs will operate across air, surface and sub-surface domains, undertaking maritime trade route protection, anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare, coastal defence, littoral combat, maritime presence and surveillance missions. Size and Displacement: The NGCs have a displacement of 3,800–4,000 tonnes, making them comparable in size to the IN’s Talwar-class frigates. Employment: The project is expected to generate approximately 72 lakh person-days of employment in shipyards and 460 lakh person-days in ancillary industries and Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) over the next 10 years. Ecosystem: The project will strengthen collaboration among DPSUs, private shipyards and Indian industrial partners, including MSMEs, while promoting the use of Made-in-India materials, equipment and indigenous technologies. Significance: The project will strengthen India’s indigenous warship design and construction capabilities and support the Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India initiatives.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 20 Daily Content PDF INTERNATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of COP17 to CBD Held from October 19 to 31, 2026 in Armenia The 17th Conference of the Parties (CoP17) to the United Nations(UN) Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was held at the Meridian Expo and Event Centre in Yerevan, Armenia, under the theme “Taking Action for Nature.” • COP17, presided over by Hambardzum Matevosyan, the Minister of Environment of the Republic of Armenia, adopted nearly 50 decisions to strengthen biodiversity conservation and implement the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). Exam Hints: ✓ Event: CoP17 to CBD ✓ Venue: Yerevan, Armenia ✓ 2026 Theme: ‘Taking Action for Nature’ ✓ COP17 President: Hambardzum Matevosyan ✓ India Represented By: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, MoEFCC ✓ Key Outcomes: o Adoption of Yerevan Pathway; o Announcement of nearly USD 2 billion in new biodiversity funding; o Adoption of nearly 50 new agenda items; among others ✓ CoP18 to CBD: Quito, Ecuador (in 2028). About CBD COP17: Aim: The two-week long conference brought together governments, international organisations, scientists, civil society, Indigenous people, youth and the private sector to examine progress, strengthen cooperation and accelerate action for biodiversity. Logo: This year’s conference logo was inspired by “Polymmatus eriwanensis(Eriwan Blue)”, a butterfly species endemic to Armenia, featuring 23 colors, which correspond to the 23 action targets of the KMGBF. Key Meetings: COP17 was held alongside the 12th Meeting of the Parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (CP-MOP12) and the 6th Meeting of the Parties to the Nagoya Protocol (NP-MOP6). Next Host: During the closing plenary session of the conference, Quito, the capital city of Ecuador has been selected to host the CoP18 to CBD in 2028. India at COP17 to CBD: Indian Representation: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), led the Indian delegation at COP17 to CBD, reaffirming India’s commitment to biodiversity conservation and highlighting its updated National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP), comprising 23 national targets and 142 indicators. • He highlighted India’s 1,134 Protected Areas, 103 Ramsar sites, 57 Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS) and 18 Biosphere Reserves (BRs), including 13 under UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Network. Key Releases: During a side event titled “From Policy to Practice: Advancing India’s Biodiversity Commitments through Innovation, Finance, ABS and OECMS” organised by the MoEFCC in partnership with India’s National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), India released the 4 key publications. • Guidelines for the Designation of India’s Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (I- OECMs) 2026; 5th National Report on Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety; The Convention on Biological Diversity Handbook: Reference Guide and Indian Perspective; and India’s Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) Success Story.

# Page 21^page=21
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 21 Daily Content PDF Key Outcomes: Yerevan Pathway: One of the key outcomes of the conference was unanimous adoption of Yerevan Pathway, a negotiated response to the first review of collective progress in the implementation of the KMGBF. • The newly adopted pathway identifies priorities to accelerate the implementation of KMBGF until 2030, including tackling nature-harmful subsidies and incentives, increasing financial, scientific and technical support for developing countries, aligning national budgets and economic decisions with the KMGBF, and strengthening implementation, monitoring, reporting and review mechanisms. Biodiversity Funding Commitment: Under the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), member nations had pledged to raise at least USD 200 billion annually from all sources by 2030, including global biodiversity finance from developed to developing countries to at least USD 30 billion by 2030. • In addition, the conference announced approximately USD 2 billion in new biodiversity funding and financial commitments, including USD 560 million under the 9th replenishment of the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and its GBF fund; USD 500 million through the Species Recovery Alliance and over USD 330 million through the Value Nature Fund. Adoption of 50 Agenda Items: Also, the conference adopted around 50 agenda items focused on: protected areas and forest biodiversity, sustainable wildlife management, invasive alien species, risk assessment of living modified organisms, marine and coastal biodiversity, synthetic biology, and biodiversity mainstreaming. Other Key Outcomes: Some of the other outcomes of the conference were: the Sevan Guidelines (for the establishment of new permanent subsidiary body on Article 8(j)); launch of a new biodiversity bond and investment incubator; and a proposal for model framework law on forests to strengthen environmental enforcement was discussed. About CoP to CBD: Background: CoP to the CBD is an apex governing body of the international treaty, adopted in 1992, for the conservation of biodiversity, the sustainable use of components of biodiversity, and equitable sharing of the benefits from the use of genetic resources. Biennial Event: The members of the CoP to the CBD meet every two years (biennially) to review the progress of the convention. • The CoP16 to the CBD was conducted in Cali, Colombia, which was paused due to lack of quorum required for biodiversity finance related agreements. • Later, the conference (COP16.2) to CBD was resumed, held from February 25 to 27, 2025 at the headquarters of Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) in Rome, Italy. Members: At present, CBD comprises 196 member countries including India. Key Protocol: KMGBF was established during COP15 held in Montreal, Canada in 2022, managed by the Global Environment Facility (GEF). • Currently, it is operational and received initial funding from Austria, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, among others, which amounted to nearly USD 382 million. About Armenia: President- Vahagn Khachaturyan Capital- Yerevan Currency- Armenian Dram (AMD)

# Page 23^page=23
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 23 Daily Content PDF Exam Hints: ✓ What? SEBI issues framework to allow REITs and InvITs to issue DRs ✓ DR Listing Venue: GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat ✓ Permitted Exchange: India INX, NSE IX ✓ Unitholders Approval: 75% of total votes cast in favour of resolution ✓ Restriction: Indian Residents barred ✓ Cooling Off Period: Reduced from 12 weeks to 8 weeks ✓ Applicability: Illiquid privately listed InvITs ✓ OFS Duration: One trading day. REITs and InvITs DRs Issuance: Depository Receipts: DRs are foreign currency-denominated instruments issued by a foreign depository against underlying units deposited with a domestic custodian. Permitted Exchanges: The permitted exchanges are: • India International Exchange (India INX) • National Stock Exchange International Exchange (NSE IX) Unitholders Approval: Fresh issuance of DRs will require prior approval from unitholders, with at least 75% of the total votes cast in favour of resolution. • Approval not required when REIT or InvIT undertakes an initial offer of units and simultaneously issues DRs. Tender: If existing unitholders transfer their units for the purpose of issuing and listing DRs, the REIT or InvIT must provide an opportunity to all existing unitholders to tender and participate in the offering. Restriction: The framework bars Indian residents from holding DRs, including through beneficial ownership. • Responsibility for ensuring compliance with this condition will lie with the DR holders and their beneficial owners. Eligibility Requirements: REITs, InvITs, their directors, promoters and partners, and unitholders transferring units must not be debarred by SEBI, wilful defaulters or fugitive economic offenders. • They must also not be associated as promoters or directors with any entity debarred from accessing the capital market. • These restrictions do not apply if the debarment period has expired by the date of filing the relevant offer document. Disclosure & Investor Eligibility: International disclosures must be filed with Indian exchanges within 24 hours, while DRs of privately placed InvITs are restricted to foreign institutional investors and corporate bodies, subject to applicable regulations. Merchant Banker (MB): The manager of a REIT and the investment manager of an InvIT will have to appoint a MB to oversee compliance with the DR issuance requirements. Fresh Issue: For a fresh issue, the initial offer document must be filed with SEBI and the stock exchanges through the merchant banker.
